name: Parties and Movements That Built Modern Nations
description: Jacobins, Chartists, Congress, Labour, the Kuomintang, the ANC and Solidarity: the organisations that seized, shared or reshaped power.

checkpoints.name: Clubs and charters
checkpoints.note: The Jacobin Club began as a debating society in revolutionary Paris and became a force that governed France in the Terror. In Britain the Chartists gathered millions of signatures for votes for working men, and the Conservative Party and America's Democratic Party took shape.

checkpoints.name: New parties
checkpoints.note: The Republican Party formed in the United States in 1854 to oppose the spread of slavery. In India the Indian National Congress first met in 1885 as a forum for educated Indians' demands.

checkpoints.name: Labour, votes and revolution
checkpoints.note: Britain's Labour Party began in 1900 to bring working people's voices into parliament, and the Women's Social and Political Union, founded in 1903, used disruptive protest for votes for women. The Muslim League formed in 1906, the Kuomintang and African National Congress in 1912, and the Bolsheviks, roots of the Soviet Communist Party, took power in 1917.

checkpoints.name: Parties in power and in struggle
checkpoints.note: The Nazi Party became Germany's ruling party in 1933 and led it into World War II. Mexico's PRI began in 1929 and held power for decades. The Chinese Communist Party won the civil war in 1949 against the Kuomintang, and in India Congress led the way to independence in 1947 as the Muslim League won Pakistan.

checkpoints.name: Movements and transitions
checkpoints.note: The Black Panther Party formed in 1966 in the United States. The Khmer Rouge took Cambodia in 1975, in Poland the trade union Solidarity challenged communist rule from 1980, and India's Bharatiya Janata Party was founded the same year. In 1994 the African National Congress won South Africa's first democratic election.
